transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

This is a common Bosch condenser/heat pump dryer issue. The light usually isn't about the container itself. It means the **pump can't move water up into the container**, so the water level in the sump at the bottom of the machine stays high and trips the float sensor. Here's what to check, roughly from easiest to most involved:

### 1. Reset it
- Switch the dryer off at the wall for **5–10 minutes**, then try again. This clears a stuck error state surprisingly often.
- After emptying the container, make sure it **clicks fully home**. If it sits slightly out, the dryer may still think it's missing or full.

### 2. Clean the fluff filters and condenser/heat exchanger
Lint buildup is the #1 cause. Fluff gets into the condensed water and clogs the pump.
- Clean the **door fluff filter(s)**.
- Open the flap at the bottom front and clean the **base filter / heat exchanger**. Some models have a self-cleaning condenser, but the base filter still needs rinsing. Rinse it under the tap until it's completely clear, let it dry, and refit it properly with the locking levers closed.
- Wipe out any fluff and water in the area where the filter sits.

### 3. Check for a drain hose
If your dryer is plumbed into a drain instead of using the container, check that the hose isn't **kinked, blocked, or pushed too far down** the standpipe. Also check that it's not more than about 1 m high.

### 4. Check for water sitting in the base
Look and feel inside the bottom compartment when the filter is out. If there's standing water or the area is very fluffy, the pump or its inlet is likely blocked. Some models have a small **pump filter or inspection cover** in this area, so check your manual (search your model number, found on the sticker inside the door, plus "manual").

To drain trapped water, you can **carefully tilt the dryer back slightly** with towels underneath. Sometimes that also frees a stuck float.

### 5. Check the container itself
Shake the container and look into the inlet. Fluff or debris inside can block the pipe where water flows in.

### If none of that works
The likely culprit is a **failed condensate pump or a stuck float switch**. That needs an engineer, or a confident DIYer, since the back or base panel has to come off. If the dryer is under ~2 years old, it should be covered under Bosch warranty. Contact Bosch service directly.

If you tell me the model number (e.g. WTH85…, WTN85…, WQG24…), I can point you to anything specific to that machine.

Container clicks in firmly, I've cleaned the filters (they were fairly clean), and there's no drain hose fitted. I can't tilt it or get to the back because it's stacked on the washer with a tower kit. The model on the manual cover starts WTG8, but the full label is on the back so I can't read it.

WTG8 is a Bosch **condenser dryer** (Serie 4/6), not a heat pump. That helps, because on these models you can **remove the condenser itself** from the front. That's the part people often miss.

### 1. Take out and rinse the condenser
The "filters" you cleaned may have been only the door fluff filter. Behind the bottom flap:
- Open the flap at the bottom front (put a towel down, since some water may come out).
- Turn the **two (or three) locking levers**.
- Pull out the **condenser block**, a fairly large rectangular unit with a handle.
- Rinse it **from all sides** under a shower or hose until water runs through clean. Fluff often hides *inside* the fins even when the faces look fine.
- Wipe the **rubber seals** on it and on the machine, since a bad seal lets water and fluff bypass it.

### 2. Clean the sump area it came out of
With the condenser out, shine a torch into the cavity:
- Remove any **fluff and standing water** at the bottom with a sponge or cloth. A turkey baster helps. The pump inlet and float sit down there, and fluff around them is the classic cause of this exact symptom.
- Gently press anything that looks like it moves or floats to make sure it isn't stuck.

Refit the condenser with the levers fully locked and the flap shut.

### 3. Check the container's inlet
With the water container pulled out, shine a torch into the slot. Look for the small spout or opening that feeds water into the container and clear any fluff around it. Also check the inlet hole on the container itself.

### 4. Check it's level
You can do this without moving anything. Put a spirit level (or a phone level app) on top of the dryer, front-to-back and side-to-side. If the stack tilts, water can pool away from the pump and trigger the light. Adjust the washer feet if needed.

### 5. Power reset
After all that, switch it off at the wall for 10 minutes, then run a short program.

### Finding the full model number
On Bosch dryers the rating label is usually **also inside the door opening**, on the frame around the drum or on the inside edge of the door. You'll want the full number (E-Nr, plus the FD number) if you need a part or an engineer.

If the light still comes on after a thorough condenser and sump clean, the **condensate pump has probably failed or seized**. It's a common part on these models. Replacing it means taking the dryer off the stack, so it's probably a job for an engineer or Bosch service. Check whether you're still within warranty first.

I took the condenser out and rinsed it, it was fairly clean. Behind a small cover by it I found some grey slimy water and fluff, and I wiped what I could reach. It then ran longer, about 60 minutes, but the light came on again. I haven't checked the level, and I'm not sure where the label is inside the door.

The longer run is a good sign. That grey slime and fluff behind the small cover is almost certainly the cause. The pump sits down there, and it's still partly clogged. You cleared enough to help, but not all of it.

### 1. Clean the sump area more thoroughly
- **Soak up all the water** with a sponge, turkey baster, or large syringe. Get it as dry as you can.
- **Flush it with warm water.** Pour some in, swirl it around with a cloth or old toothbrush, then soak it up again. Repeat until it comes out clear. Warm water loosens slime much better than wiping alone.
- Use a **torch** and feel around the edges and corners. Fluff tends to collect around the pump inlet and the float, which may be out of sight.
- Don't push anything sharp into openings, since the pump impeller is easy to damage.

### 2. Test the pump directly
After cleaning:
1. Pour **about a cup of clean water** into the sump area.
2. Refit the cover, condenser, and flap, and put the container in.
3. Start a drying program. After a few minutes, pull the container out and look.

**If the water has moved into the container, the pump works**, and the problem was the blockage. Also listen near the bottom for a short humming or buzzing sound. That's the pump running.

**If the water is still sitting in the sump**, the pump is seized or failed, or the pipe from the pump to the container is blocked. That's an engineer job.

### 3. Check the level
This takes 30 seconds. Put a spirit level or a phone level app on top of the dryer, front-to-back and side-to-side. A tilt toward the back can make water pool away from the pump and trigger the light early.

### 4. Finding the label
On Bosch dryers, with the door open, check these spots with a torch:
- the **frame around the door opening**, especially the bottom edge or the sides
- the **inside edge of the door** itself

Look for a sticker with **E-Nr** (the full model number, e.g. WTG86400GB/03) and **FD** (production date). You'll need both if you call Bosch or order a pump.

If the cup-of-water test shows the pump isn't moving water after a good clean, it's time to call Bosch service or a local appliance engineer.
Ok, I'll try the cup of water test. I don't really know what a humming pump sounds like though, so I'll just check the container afterwards. Will report back.

Checking the container is the more reliable test anyway. A few tips:

- **Give it 5–10 minutes** of running before checking. The pump usually kicks in once the float detects water, but it may not be instant.
- **A cup is plenty.** Too much might trigger the light right away.
- **Compare with what you poured in.** If most of it ended up in the container, the pump works. If only a little did, the pump may be weak or partly blocked.
- If the light comes on early in the test, check the container and the sump before restarting. That tells you whether water moved or stayed put.

Good luck, and let me know what happens.
Ok, will do. I'll run it for about 10 minutes and then check the container and let you know.

Sounds good. One small note: the pump may run in short bursts rather than continuously, so if there's only a little water in the container at 10 minutes, check the sump too before drawing conclusions.

Talk soon.
Ok, I'll go and do the test now and come back with what I find.
